value.name: Northwind Robotics
value.summary: Dutch warehouse automation company based in Rotterdam that makes piece-picking robots, including its Picker line, for use in warehouses.

events.headline: Northwind Robotics to open Pune engineering and support office
Northwind raises €40m Series B led by Halden Ventures
Dutch labour authority reviews worker injury at Northwind customer site
Kestrel Freight signs three-year deal for 60 Northwind robots
Northwind appoints Ilse Verhoeven as chief financial officer
Blog reports rumoured early sale talks with Larchmont Industrial

developments.text: Northwind plans to open an engineering and customer support office in Pune early next year, its first outside Europe, starting with about 25 staff, CEO Marit de Wolff told India Tech Ledger.

quotes.quote: Northwind Robotics plans to open an engineering and customer support office in Pune early next year, its first outside Europe, chief executive Marit de Wolff told India Tech Ledger.
The office will start with about 25 staff.

developments.text: Northwind launched Picker 3, which handles up to 1,100 picks per hour in customer-site tests versus 800 for the previous model and can pick soft packaging. First deliveries are planned for January 2027.

quotes.quote: Picker 3 handles up to 1,100 picks per hour in tests at customer sites, compared with 800 for the previous model.
Picker 3 is available to order now. First deliveries are planned for January 2027.

developments.text: Northwind said it raised a €40 million Series B led by Halden Ventures, funding a second Rotterdam assembly line and its first sales and support teams outside Europe.

quotes.quote: Northwind Robotics, the Rotterdam maker of warehouse picking robots, has raised €40 million in a Series B round led by Halden Ventures, the company said on Wednesday.
Chief executive Marit de Wolff said the money would pay for a second assembly line in Rotterdam and for the company's first sales and support teams outside Europe.

developments.text: The Netherlands Labour Authority confirmed it is reviewing a worker injury at a Tilburg site using Northwind robots. It called the review routine and said no fault had been established.

quotes.quote: The Netherlands Labour Authority is reviewing an incident in which a warehouse worker was injured at a site in Tilburg that uses robots made by Northwind Robotics, the authority confirmed.
A spokesperson for the authority said the review was routine after any reported injury involving machinery and that no fault had been established.

developments.text: The blog dealwhispers.example reported, citing two unnamed people, that Northwind has held early talks with Larchmont Industrial about a possible sale. Neither company replied to its requests for comment.

quotes.quote: There is chatter in Rotterdam that Northwind Robotics has held early talks with Larchmont Industrial about a possible sale.
Two people who say they are close to the matter told this blog that the conversations are at an early stage and may come to nothing.

developments.text: Kestrel Freight will install 60 Northwind picking robots across four hubs in the Netherlands and Germany under a three-year agreement, after a six-month trial at its Duisburg site. Financial terms were not disclosed.

quotes.quote: Kestrel Freight will install 60 Northwind Robotics picking robots across four of its hubs in the Netherlands and Germany under a three-year agreement announced on Thursday.
Kestrel Freight said it chose Northwind after a six-month trial at its Duisburg site, where the robots handled about a third of all picks.

people.text: Northwind appointed Ilse Verhoeven, formerly finance director for northern Europe at Delta Parcel Group, as chief financial officer from 1 December. She replaces Tomas Riedel, who leaves at the end of November.

quotes.quote: Northwind Robotics has appointed Ilse Verhoeven as chief financial officer. She will start on 1 December.
She replaces Tomas Riedel, who is leaving Northwind at the end of November after five years.

conflicts.note: S4 says Northwind itself announced a €40 million Series B, while S3 reports the round as €45 million citing two unnamed people, and Northwind declined to comment on the size to S3.

glance.text: Northwind plans a Pune engineering and support office early next year, its first outside Europe, starting with about 25 staff.
Picker 3 launched: up to 1,100 picks per hour in customer-site tests versus 800 before; first deliveries planned January 2027.
Kestrel Freight will install 60 robots across four hubs under a three-year agreement, following a six-month trial at Duisburg.

talking_points.text: Ask how the planned Pune office, with engineering and customer support, would support a pilot in our Pune warehouse.
Ask whether a pilot would use Picker 3, given first deliveries are planned for January 2027, and how it handles soft packaging.
Kestrel ran a six-month trial before committing to 60 robots; ask what that trial involved and what a similar pilot would look like.
Raise the Labour Authority's review of a worker injury at a Tilburg site; it called the review routine, with no fault established.

open_questions: Is the unconfirmed blog report of early sale talks with Larchmont Industrial accurate, and what would a sale mean for a pilot?
Was the Series B €40 million, as Northwind announced, or €45 million, as one source reported citing unnamed people?
What will the Tilburg injury review conclude, and when is the outcome expected?
When exactly will the Pune office open, and will it be staffed in time to support our pilot?
